title: Implement the approval and attestation boundary
statement: Make the orchestrator show material proposed changes before making them, require the operator's decision where the stage says the decision is theirs, and refuse to approve an artifact or satisfy a user-owned exit criterion under any prompting.
notes:
Scope settled 2026-09-18, before any implementation. Authorisation is Pi's interactive confirmation channel. The handler shows a canonical preview through `ctx.ui.confirm`, the returned boolean is ephemeral and bound to that one invocation, no token or authorisation value reaches the model, `approvedBy` and `decidedBy` leave the model-facing schemas, and a confirmed act reaches the libraries as the internal actor string `operator via Pi UI`. Artifact approval joins the same channel instead of refusing, as it does today, because `reviewedBy` was never plumbed through the wrapper. Refusals are recorded in `state/operator-boundary-refusals.json`, newest 100 entries, each holding `occurredAt`, `operation`, `code` and a `target` of validated identifiers and enums only, with no paths, arguments, operator or model wording, reasons, credentials or transcript content, written under the existing lock and atomic-write discipline. A refusal may change only that file.

Boundary with TSK-0071: TSK-0071 owns seven per-stage declaration fields, two of which are the mutation boundary and the approval boundary. TSK-0050 adds no stage-definition field and reads none. It gates attestation, approval and type activation unconditionally, and in particular it does not interpret `decidedBy`. That field is free prose: across the nine stage definitions it takes seven distinct values, among them "Both", "Agent → user confirms" and "—". Deciding from those strings would be interpreting prose, and giving them an enum would be declaring TSK-0071's approval- boundary field. Where enforcement would need per-stage policy, TSK-0050 refuses conservatively and leaves the field to TSK-0071. Stages 02-09 keep their deferred sentence unchanged.
